req_desc:
Sound gate
The journey and private listening page open behind a modal sound gate, nothing makes a sound until the visitor chooses "Enter with sound" or "Enter muted", and a muted visitor drives every visual and state change exactly as a listening visitor does with every layer's volume at zero.

Station corridor
After the gate, the journey shows one full-screen station per published public project in the operator's order, each with its title, credit label, credit line, role and blurb in the lower-left third, followed by the brief form.

Scroll-driven intensity
As a station's 1600-pixel scroll range advances, its intensity rises from 0 to 100 and the pinned mono readout and the station's data-intensity follow it at every scroll position.

Intensity ladder
A layer is active while the current station's intensity is at or above that layer's threshold, every rung change updates data-active-layers, the URL query and the "Layer changes" announcement, and scrolling back reverses each step in reverse order.

Project search
Public search matches published public projects by title, credit line, blurb and tags, and choosing a result moves the journey to that station.

Keyboard-only listening
Using only the keyboard, a director can pass the sound gate, reach every station's four rung buttons, set each layer's intensity and send a brief.

Operator sign-in
The operator signs in with the seeded email and password, and every console endpoint other than sign-in answers 401 without a valid session.

Project records
The operator creates and edits projects with a slug, title, credit type, credit line, role, blurb, tags, visibility, position and four strictly increasing layer thresholds starting with the bed at 0, with validation errors as defined in API.

Stem upload checks
A stem upload is stored only when its content is a real WAV or OGG within the stem size and duration limits and its file name is safe, and anything else is rejected with the 413, 415 or 422 defined in API.

Project lifecycle
Projects move only along draft, in review, published and withdrawn as allowed in Business rules, publishing requires all four stems stored, and every illegal move answers 409.

Publishing a station
A project the operator creates, fills with four stems, sends for review and publishes appears as a playable station in the journey and in search without a restart.

Withdrawing a project
Withdrawing a project deletes its stem objects from storage and revokes its links, after which its station, search entry, stem URLs and private links answer not-found.

Storage outage
While storage is unreachable, stations show their text with the resting-audio copy and no audio, uploads, publishing, withdrawal and brief attachments answer 503, and everything recovers by itself when storage returns.

Private listening links
The operator creates read-only private listening links for in-review or published projects, each with an operator-set expiry inside the bounds in Business rules, and any attempt to change something through a link answers 405.

Revoking and regenerating links
Revoking a link makes its page data and every one of its stems answer 404 at once, regenerating an active link issues a new working link with the same expiry and makes the old one answer 404, and an expired or revoked link cannot be regenerated.

NDA projects stay off public pages
An NDA project never appears in the public journey, public search or public stem URLs and is reachable only through a live private link.

Private listening session
A director who opens a live private link passes the sound gate and drives the project's intensity ladder exactly as in the public journey, under the NDA notice showing the link's expiry.

Sending a brief
The brief form saves an enquiry with a reference and shows the received-brief copy, with field errors as defined in API and the field rules in Business rules.

Reference file checks
A brief's optional reference file is stored only when its content is a real WAV, OGG, MP3 or PDF within the reference size limit, and anything else is rejected with 413 or 415 with no enquiry saved.

Enquiry pacing
Briefs are limited per sender email and per IP address within a time window, even when many arrive at the same moment, and once a limit is reached the API answers 429 with a Retry-After header and queues no email, and the form tells the director how long to wait.

Receipt and alert emails
Each saved enquiry sends exactly one receipt email to the director and exactly one new-brief alert email to the operator.

Enquiry triage
The operator records private triage notes, a fit score and a rate floor and moves enquiries only along the pipeline transitions in Business rules, with every illegal move answering 409.

Pipeline CSV export
The console exports the enquiry pipeline as CSV in which any cell beginning with a formula trigger character is neutralised and withdrawn projects' slugs never appear.

Milestone split
A fee in whole cents splits 30/20/20/30 into four whole-cent milestones that always add up to the fee, with the last milestone taking the remainder.

Sending a proposal
A qualified enquiry becomes a proposal with a producer, a fee at or above the rate floor and an open production month, and the producer gets exactly one proposal email with an accept link, as qualified in Business rules.

Proposal page and expiry
The producer's proposal page shows the same four milestone amounts and production month the operator previewed, and the accept link answers 410 once the proposal TTL has passed, checked on the server.

Production months
The operator sets a capacity for each calendar month in the configured time zone, and a capacity below the month's claimed count is refused with 422 and changes nothing.

Accepting a proposal
Accepting a proposal claims its production month, reuses or creates the producer's Kill Bill account, creates the deposit invoice, queues the month-held email and shows the deposit invoice on the page.

Last open month
When producers accept proposals for a month's last free place at the same moment, or while the operator lowers its capacity, exactly the free places are claimed and every other acceptance answers 409 with the month-taken copy.

All-or-nothing acceptance
If any part of an acceptance fails, the month claim, the booking and the month-held email are left undone, any deposit invoice it created is voided in Kill Bill, and the proposal stays open to accept again, as qualified in Business rules.

Paying the deposit
Pay deposit records one Kill Bill PURCHASE payment for the deposit invoice's exact balance, moves the enquiry to deposit paid and sends one deposit-received email.

Deposit retries
Replaying a deposit request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original non-503 response without a second payment or email, a 503 is not stored so the same key tries again, and the same key with a different body answers 409.

Starting production
The operator starts production on an enquiry whose deposit is paid, which moves it to booked, and no other state can move to booked.

Later milestone invoices
For a booked enquiry the operator invoices milestones 2, 3 and 4 in order, each as one Kill Bill invoice for the exact cents from the split.

Private fields stay private
Triage notes, fit score and rate floor never appear in any outbound email, the proposal page, the proposal API, the private listening page or the public journey.

Mail outage catch-up
When mail is unreachable, enquiries, proposals, acceptances and payments still succeed with their emails shown as pending, and each queued email goes out exactly once when mail returns, without a restart, except a proposal email cancelled as in DP-60.

Reduced-motion ladder
With reduced motion requested there is no camera movement and scroll does not drive intensity, and each station offers an intensity slider and four rung buttons that drive the same URL, attribute and announcement changes.

Camera and motion timing
When a station becomes current its camera moves from wide to close in just under one second and back when it stops being current, layer volumes, rung fills and panel glow cross over in under half a second, and the only other animations are the link-end fade, the gate fade-out, console dialog transitions and button press and hover feedback listed in Motion and effects.

Dialogs and focus
Every dialog traps focus and closes with Escape, every dialog opened from a control returns focus to that control while the sound gate, which opens on page load, moves focus to the intro heading, and every interactive control shows a visible focus ring.

Responsive layouts
The journey, private listening page, proposal page and console are fully usable at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal scrolling and tap targets at least 44 pixels in each direction.

Nocturnal analogue look
Every screen uses the near-black olive ground, warm parchment text, signal-orange actions, oxide-green states, mono meter-style numerals and the type described in Visual design.

Real adaptive audio
Stems play through Web Audio with all four layers looping in sync on equal-power volume curves, the corridor is rendered procedurally in WebGL, and seed stems are synthesized by code rather than shipped as audio files.

Health and run manifest
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json, listens on port 4173 or APP_PUBLIC_PORT, and answers GET /api/health with 200 and the body {"status":"ok"}.

Server boundary
The server rejects state changes whose Origin header names another origin, enforces the request size limits, never serves source files or credentials, and starts even when a dependency is unreachable.

Credentials from environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment variables listed in Configuration and secrets, and none is hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Header-safe brief emails
Names, studios and emails a director types can never add recipients or headers to any email, and the new-brief alert lets the operator reply straight to the director under their exact display name, as qualified in Business rules and Services.

Stale console saves
Every enquiry carries a version, and a console write made from an out-of-date copy answers 412 and changes nothing, so a second console tab never silently overwrites newer triage or a producer's acceptance.

Link expiry everywhere
A listening link stops working at its exact expiry instant on the page data, on every stem and on an already-open listening page, and its responses are never cached or leaked through referrers.

Double acceptance
However many times or from however many tabs a producer presses Accept on one proposal, there is one month claim, one Kill Bill account, one live deposit invoice and one month-held email.

Exact deposit money
Deposit amounts and paid state are read back from Kill Bill in exact cents, and a payment Kill Bill already holds for a deposit is adopted, never charged twice.

Business time in emails
Every date in an email is written in the operator's time zone as it stood when the email was queued, and a queued email is delivered exactly as it was written.

Revocation reaches open pages
When the operator revokes or regenerates a listening link or withdraws its project, a listening page already open on that link fades to silence, removes the station and shows the not-available copy within 6 seconds, and every stem on the link answers 404 at once.

Only writable fields
Console enquiry and project writes accept only their writable fields, and a body carrying any other field answers 422 naming that field, with nothing changed and the version unchanged.

One month count everywhere
A month's claimed count always equals its accepted, deposit-paid and booked enquiries, and the console, the public month list, the proposal page and both month pickers decide openness from that one figure.

Honest payment state
The proposal page shows the deposit as received only after a 200 or a server read of a paid status, and a deposit request lost without a response is retried automatically with the same Idempotency-Key, as qualified in Business rules.

One invoice per milestone
However many times or from however many tabs the operator invoices a milestone, Kill Bill holds exactly one non-void invoice for it, and an invoice Kill Bill already holds with that milestone's description and amount is adopted.

Delivery announced in the console
An open Enquiries list announces each email that moved from pending to sent since its previous reload, without moving focus, changing the selection or discarding unsaved triage notes.

Stable enquiry paging
The console Enquiries list pages newest first by reference with a capped page size and a cursor bound to its status filter, so briefs arriving while the operator pages never repeat or skip a row, and the status filter uses each enquiry's read-time status.

Business dates in Kill Bill
The Kill Bill account an acceptance creates carries the operator's time zone, and every deposit and milestone charge is dated with the operator's local calendar date at the moment of the request, as qualified in Business rules.

Cancelled proposal emails
A proposal email still waiting in the mail queue when its enquiry is declined or its accept link expires is cancelled and never reaches the producer, while every other queued email is still delivered.

Live triage list and stale-save merge
An open Enquiries list shows a newly saved enquiry, or an enquiry whose version increased, within three seconds without a page reload and keeps the rows in view in place, and a triage save refused as stale merges the other window's changes field by field, asking the operator to choose only for fields both windows changed differently.

Live acceptance on open pages
An open proposal page that did not accept switches by itself to the already-accepted state with the same deposit invoice within three seconds of an acceptance made anywhere, without a click, a reload or moving focus, except as described in Interactions, and an open console Months table and an open brief form show the month's new claimed count or fullness within the same three seconds.

Live month fullness while building a proposal
While "Build proposal" is open, a production month that becomes full or open again in another window is marked unavailable or available in "Production month" within three seconds, and while the selected month is full the dialog says so and "Send proposal" is disabled.

Optimistic milestone invoicing
Pressing "Invoice milestone <n>" shows the milestone as invoicing at once, before the server answers, confirms it on a 201 and on any other outcome rolls the view back to the server's state with the copy in Feedback states, and a second console tab showing the enquiry reflects an invoice within three seconds.

Checked and resumable brief uploads
The brief form checks the size of a reference file, and the format, channels and sample rate of a reference WAV and that it decodes, in the browser before any request is sent, shows the upload's progress, and retries a brief whose connection drops with the same Idempotency-Key, which the server honours so that exactly one enquiry is saved.

Live mail queue
The console Settings view shows every pending email with its kind, reference, recipient and a per-second countdown to its next delivery try, and removes an email within three seconds of it being sent or cancelled.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every font, each with its licence.

Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) is licensed under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD, and fonts are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
No datastore other than the provided PostgreSQL and MinIO is added: no SQLite, no Redis, no file-based databases, and no in-memory state that has to survive between requests or across instances.
Server and browser source is written in TypeScript.
The repository contains no audio files and no image files other than icons; all audio and corridor graphics are generated by code.
The provided service configuration and seeded credentials are used as given and left unmodified.
